relations.subject: Paul Demiéville
relations.evidence: Demiéville was named a resident of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (French School of the Far East) in Hanoi, where he lived from 1920 to 1924.

relations.subject: Paul Demiéville
relations.evidence: In 1924 he moved to southeast China, where he taught Sanskrit and philosophy at the University of Amoy (modern Xiamen University).

relations.subject: Paul Demiéville
relations.evidence: In 1926 Demiéville moved to Tokyo, Japan, where he became director of the Maison Franco-Japonaise (French-Japanese House)

relations.subject: Paul Demiéville
relations.evidence: In 1945 he became director of the 4th Section of the École Pratique des Haute Études and taught Buddhist philosophy there until 1956.

relations.subject: Paul Demiéville
relations.role: Chair of Chinese Language and Literature
relations.evidence: selected to replace Henri Maspero as Chair of Chinese Language and Literature at the Collège de France – Maspero having died in the Buchenwald concentration camp in 1945 – and held that position until his retirement in 1964.

relations.subject: Paul Demiéville
relations.evidence: From 1945 to 1975, Demiéville served as the French co-editor of the prominent sinology journal T'oung Pao
